subject: Sea dragon legacy baseline and cinematic presentation
scope: Legacy anatomy baseline only; current replacement anatomy is not graded or approved here.

evidence.inspected: All 24 original baseline-sequence-v001 frames; all 18 baseline-studio-v001 frames; corrected baseline-studio-v002 pose-21.5 and flight-clay-45.
evidence.validity: Studio v001 pose-21.5 retained world-water clipping after root normalization. Its sliced lower jaw/belly/wing is a harness artifact, excluded from anatomy scoring. Corrected v002 restores full anatomy. Baseline source hashes are recorded by capture packets.

findings.issue: Round helmet-like skull and separate oval muzzle sit on a near-uniform tubular body. White angular throat plate and teal pectoral lobes read as stacked pieces, rather than the target's integrated skull-neck-shoulder mass.
Wings read as radial triangular fans starting directly on the torso. A load-bearing bent upper arm, elbow and wrist hierarchy is not legible.

Large membrane regions disappear in clay45 while spars remain. Beauty retains more membrane. This suggests side/winding or clay-override dependence; do not claim a literal beauty hole without diagnosis. New macro must pass both sides with consistent visible surfaces.
Precontact folded wings are overlapping triangular sheets with exposed spars laid against the body, rather than a coherent folded limb. This persists independently of the corrected clipping artifact.
Eruption is a nearly straight pointed pillar with weak folded-appendage bulk. Pose10.5 also crops the tail in the study; enlarge study framing before relying on whole-body containment.
Thin triangular fluke and straight needle horns do not preserve the inferred reference's curved volumetric forms.

counterPolicy: Retire the inherited legacy representation; this baseline is not a review or failure of the separately authorized new-anatomy family1. Keep the new build-contract family/review counters intact.
requiredMacroGates: Whole coupled creature: continuous shaped torso/tapering tail, integrated neck/skull/jaw and owned shoulder sockets. No collar slot, throat cone, ball-skull assembly or disconnected shoulder lobes.
Legible upper arm/elbow/wrist/finger hierarchy and a continuous curved scalloped membrane; opposite views and clay must not lose required surfaces.
Folded, unfurl, glide, bank and dive poses preserve appendage identity and believable length. No overlapping shredded panels, plane collapse, spikes or inflation used as deployment.
Tail fluke and horns retain curved volume in profile, top and opposite views.
Inspect fixed nine-angle flight orbit, both clay opposites and seven timed poses with water clipping and VFX disabled only in isolated studio; keep full creature in frame.

Every critical category and required view >=0.85. One bounded correction per family must improve weakest category >=0.10 with no regression >0.05. Hard veto or score <0.50 retires family; maximum two families/four reviews per contract.

findings: At3s dark shaft overlays foreground buildings/route; at7.4s masks emerging dragon. This is a separate rendering veto, not an anatomy defect.
Close shaft at6.5/7.15 cuts abruptly to remote island at7.4; further framing changes at10.2 and13.4. Flight13.4/15/16.5 leaves the subject around one-quarter frame width in mostly empty sky.
Sky-dome edge is visibly clipped at top-left16.5.
21.5/21.8/22.2 body progressively disappears, but baseline splash/clipping elevation is inconsistent with actual ocean. Authoritative surface contact must be recaptured after root correction.
21.8/22.2 solid concentric torus bands and tall straight cones read as graphic rings and spikes, with no convincing curved crown and falling droplets.
22.6 damage close-up is obscured by broad translucent wash geometry;23.5 exposes a roofless house but airborne rectangular debris does not prove settling.
requiredEvidence: Continuous deterministic full23.5s clip and portrait counterpart; exact frames alone cannot approve speed, easing or continuity.
Dense paired frames around7.18,10.2,13.4,19.2,21.45 and22.5 to verify no camera or pose jump; preserve gameplay phase boundaries.
Water-contact frames21.35,21.45,21.6,21.9,22.2,22.5,22.6,22.68 at actual shared-ocean elevation, showing head then torso then tail submerge.
Visible curved impact crown, broken foam arcs and descending drops, then a receding wave reaching the correctly bound damaged house; rubble fall/settle through aftermath.
Reduced-motion and low-tier capture must retain story readability.

followupPresentationOnly.resolved: Stencil-enabled shaft is confined to pond at3s and7.4s. The foreground-cylinder veto is resolved in these study pixels.
followupPresentationOnly.unchanged: Distant flight framing, visible sky-dome edge16.5 and rigid torus/cone impact remain visible. No current anatomy approval is implied.
followupPresentationOnly.productionLimit: Root reports matching production stencil enablement; this review directly verifies study pixels only.
